title: Time series forecasting using singular spectrum analysis, fuzzy systems and neural networks
author: Sulandari, Subanar, et al.

steps.title: Install required software
steps.instruction: Install and load the R package **RSSA** (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/Rssa) for SSA‑LRF, the R package **forecast** for comparison models, and the MATLAB **ntstool** toolbox for neural‑network modelling. Obtain the source code for the four fuzzy‑time‑series (WFTS) procedures (Chen, Yu, Cheng, Lee) from the article’s supplementary material.

steps.title: Fit SSA‑LRF model
steps.instruction: Apply the SSA‑LRF algorithm to the original time‑series data using RSSA:

substeps.instruction: 1.1 Choose a window length L that is roughly the middle of the series length and proportional to the seasonal period (e.g., L ≈ 12 for monthly data).
1.2 Construct the trajectory matrix from the series with the chosen L.
1.3 Perform singular value decomposition (SVD) on the trajectory matrix.
1.4 Separate the resulting elementary matrices into two groups – signal and noise – aided by the w‑correlation matrix if desired.
1.5 Reconstruct the signal and noise series by diagonal averaging of the respective groups.
1.6 Compute the forecast values for the signal component using the linear recurrent formula provided by SSA‑LRF.

steps.title: Obtain SSA‑LRF residuals
steps.instruction: Subtract the reconstructed signal series from the original series to obtain the residual series (the noise component) that will be modelled further.

steps.title: Model residuals with neural network
steps.instruction: Train a feed‑forward neural network on the SSA‑LRF residuals using ntstool:

substeps.instruction: 2.1 Design the network architecture: for univariate forecasting use one output unit; select the number of input units and hidden‑layer nodes appropriate for the data.
2.2 Choose activation functions – **tansig** for the hidden layer (suitable because residuals contain both negative and positive values) and **purelin** for the output layer.
2.3 Train the network with the Levenberg‑Marquardt back‑propagation algorithm to obtain the input‑to‑hidden and hidden‑to‑output weight matrices.
2.4 Use the trained network to forecast the residual series.

steps.title: Combine SSA‑LRF and NN forecasts
steps.instruction: Add the SSA‑LRF signal forecast (Step 1.6) to the neural‑network residual forecast (Step 4.4) to obtain the final hybrid forecast for the original time series.

steps.title: Model residuals with fuzzy time series
steps.instruction: Alternatively, model the SSA‑LRF residuals with a weighted fuzzy‑time‑series (WFTS) approach:

substeps.instruction: 3.1 Define the universe of discourse U = [Dmin − D1, Dmax + D2], where Dmin and Dmax are the minimum and maximum residual values, and D1, D2 are positive numbers chosen by the analyst.
3.2 Partition U into n equal intervals (u1,…,un) of length l = ((Dmax + D2) − (Dmin − D1)) / n.
3.3 Construct fuzzy sets A1,…,An, each centred on its interval; the membership function of Ai peaks in ui and tapers to zero in neighbouring intervals as described in the article.
3.4 Fuzzify each residual value by assigning it to the appropriate fuzzy set(s) using the membership functions.
3.5 Derive fuzzy logical relationships (FLRs) from the fuzzified series using one of the four methods (Chen, Yu, Cheng, Lee).
3.6 Compute the residual forecast from the FLRs according to the selected method.
3.7 Add the SSA‑LRF signal forecast (Step 1.6) to the fuzzy‑based residual forecast (Step 3.6) to obtain the final hybrid forecast.
